value.body: An industrial or product designer shapes physical things people use, from kitchen appliances and furniture to medical devices and vehicles. Design studios, consumer-product makers, automotive and electronics firms hire them. Work moves from research and sketches to 3D models and prototypes, in close contact with engineering and manufacturing teams.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Des in Industrial or Product Design

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Sketching, 3D CAD and rendering software, workshop prototyping

items.label: Design applications filed in India
items.note: Industrial design registrations cover a product's shape and look

items.label: Students in B.Des. programmes
items.note: All design specialisations, not only industrial/product design

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join a design studio or the in-house design team of a manufacturer, typically after a final-year industry project or internship. A portfolio showing process (research, sketches, models) is central to hiring.

value.title: At a glance
items: Common next roles: senior designer, design lead, CMF (colour, material, finish) or design-research roles.
Jobs cluster in manufacturing and design hubs.
Some designers move into UI/UX, as research and prototyping skills carry over.

value.title: Design applications filed in India
value.note: Filings by all applicants, including foreign firms; not a count of designers or jobs.
